messages.text: I’ll look for Codex’s local session storage first, then filter for threads tied to this repo path and export them into a visible folder here. I’ll keep the extraction read-only until I’ve mapped the format, then write the archive files into the repo.

content.text: I’ll look for Codex’s local session storage first, then filter for threads tied to this repo path and export them into a visible folder here. I’ll keep the extraction read-only until I’ve mapped the format, then write the archive files into the repo.

messages.text: I found the important pieces: Codex has local JSONL rollouts under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/` plus a `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl`, and there are also two files in `~/.codex/archived_sessions/`. Next I’m going to inspect the metadata and message shape so the export preserves useful roles, dates, titles, and source paths.

content.text: I found the important pieces: Codex has local JSONL rollouts under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/` plus a `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl`, and there are also two files in `~/.codex/archived_sessions/`. messages.text: There is a proper local thread table too: `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite` has `threads` with `title`, `cwd`, archive flags, git info, and the rollout JSONL path. That’s better than guessing from filename alone, so I’m using the database as the source of truth and the JSONL files as the message bodies.

messages.text: I’ve got enough confidence to export now. I’m going to create a visible `Codex_Conversation_History` folder in this repo with one Markdown transcript and one normalized JSON file per Codex thread, plus an index and README; screenshots embedded in prompts will be extracted into an `attachments` folder instead of leaving giant base64 blobs in the JSON.
